get.summary: List products with filters, variants and good price
get.description:
Paginated product listing across the device catalogs. Parent rows come back with their variants nested and a computed goodPrice; when a search term is given with no deviceType, every catalog table is searched and merged.

**Notes:** Cross-table search caps each catalog at 100 matched rows before merging and paginating in memory.

post.summary: Create a device variant under a parent product
post.description:
Creates a child variant (storage/RAM for Mobile, Tablet, Mac; case size for Watch; price-only for Laptop and Desktop) inheriting brand, model, images and SEO fields from the parent product. Same-spec duplicates within a modelCode family are rejected with 409.

**Notes:** No handler-level auth check. Sets device buy-back prices shown to customers, so it is price-sensitive. Duplicate detection only covers Mobile, Tablet, Mac and Watch (keyed on modelCode plus specs, with missing specs treated as 0) - Laptop and Desktop have no duplicate guard. Laptop and Desktop variants persist only price/classId; their storage, RAM and variant title fields are commented out in the code. An unrecognised deviceType falls through every branch and returns success:true with data null.

_Source: `app/api/variants/route.ts`_

_Auth: `none`_

409.description: A variant with the same specs already exists in this model family

example.error: Samsung Galaxy S26 5G already has a 512GB / 12GB RAM variant at ₹60000. Edit that variant'…

put.description:
Updates a variant's specs and price in the catalog matching deviceType. Mobile, Tablet and Mac update storage, RAM, price, class and variant copy; Watch updates size; Laptop and Desktop update price and class only.

**Notes:** No handler-level auth check. Price-sensitive: this is the intended way to re-price an existing variant rather than creating a duplicate. Fields are written unconditionally, so omitting storage/ram/price on a Mobile variant sets them to undefined/null rather than leaving them unchanged. An unrecognised deviceType returns success:true with data null and changes nothing.

_Source: `app/api/variants/route.ts`_

_Auth: `none`_

delete.description:
Deletes a variant row from the catalog table matching the deviceType query parameter.

**Notes:** No handler-level auth check. Hard delete with no parent/variant guard - passing a parent product's id deletes the parent row itself. An unrecognised deviceType still returns success:true without deleting anything.

_Source: `app/api/variants/route.ts`_

_Auth: `none`_

MessageEnvelope.description: Message-only envelope `{ message }`; used for both success and failure responses.

SuccessMessageEnvelope.description: Envelope `{ success, message }`; `success` is `true` on 2xx and `false` on error responses.

Unauthorized.description: Unauthenticated - no valid admin session (NextAuth cookie), or the expected token/secret is missing or wrong. For operations whose description says *reconstructed from source*, only the status code was detected in the audit; the body shape shown is the codebase convention, not verified per route.

cookieAuth.name: next-auth.session-token
cookieAuth.description: NextAuth JWT session cookie from logging in to the admin panel. On HTTPS the cookie name is `__Secure-next-auth.session-token`.

cronBearer.description: `LINODE_CRON_SECRET` as a bearer token — every cron job goes through `assertCronAuth` in `lib/linode/cron-auth.ts`, which reads only this variable (despite some jobs being non-Linode).

unverifiedAccessToken.name: Authorization
unverifiedAccessToken.description: Legacy customer routes: an `accessToken` cookie or an `Authorization` header must be PRESENT, but the value is never verified. Not real authentication.

adsWebhookSecret.name: x-webhook-secret
adsWebhookSecret.description: `ADS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, sent either as the `x-webhook-secret` header or as a `secret` field in the JSON body. If the env var is unset the route rejects every call with 401 (it does not fall through to unauthenticated access).

webhookSecret.name: x-webhook-secret
webhookSecret.description: Generic `x-webhook-secret` header check for an inbound webhook.

cronSecretBearer.description: `CRON_SECRET` as a bearer token, compared with `bearerMatches` in `lib/auth/secret-compare.ts`. Distinct from `cronBearer`, which uses `LINODE_CRON_SECRET`.
